title: Huma Qureshi Doesn't Say a Word in 'Baby Do Die Do' — and That's the Whole Terrifying Point
excerpt: Bollywood's first deaf-and-mute hitwoman arrives July 3. No dialogue, no warning, no mercy — just a woman the underworld never saw coming.
body:
The trailer opens on a woman nobody notices. That, it turns out, is the deadliest thing about her.

<youtube>https://youtube.com/watch?v=2rQCZKoaEhc</youtube>

**Huma Qureshi** plays Baby Karmarkar, a deaf-and-mute woman threading through the chaos of Mumbai by day and slipping out into its underbelly by night — a contract executioner whose own family has no idea where she vanishes to after dark. She doesn't speak. She doesn't need to. The tagline lands like a slap: *she can't hear you.* And by the time anyone realises what Baby is, it's already too late.

This is **Baby Do Die Do**, and it might be the most quietly audacious swing of Huma Qureshi's career. The two-minute-twenty-seven-second trailer dropped this week ahead of the film's July 3 theatrical release, and the internet did exactly what you'd hope — it leaned in. "Seeing Huma Qureshi as India's first desi hitwoman brings a unique twist to the thriller genre," one viewer wrote, "and the quirky title only adds to the curiosity." Bollywood has given us assassins and avengers, but a silent one? A woman who weaponises the very thing society pities her for? That's new.

What makes the trailer work isn't the body count — it's the restraint. Director **Nachiket Samant** has been clear that he wasn't chasing a loud, explosive actioner. "When we started making this film, the idea was never to make a loud thriller," he said. "We wanted the suspense to come from the people and the emotions. Baby doesn't speak, but she's probably the most expressive character in the film. The trailer gives you a peek into her world, but trust me, we've held back the biggest surprises."

For Qureshi — last seen commanding the screen in *Heeramandi* — the role demanded she throw away her loudest tool. No monologues to hide behind, no verbal sparring. Every flicker of menace, every crack of grief had to live in her eyes, her shoulders, the set of her jaw.

> "Baby challenged me in ways I didn't expect. She doesn't rely on words, so every emotion had to come from within. There were days when saying nothing felt much harder than delivering pages of dialogue." — Huma Qureshi

That's the line that should make you book a ticket. Anyone can fire a gun on screen. Holding an entire thriller together in silence — owning a frame without a single line of dialogue — is a different order of difficulty, and the trailer suggests Qureshi has the chops to pull it off.

There's a sweet backstory humming underneath the bloodshed, too. **Baby Do Die Do** marks the debut production venture of siblings Huma Qureshi and **Saqib Saleem** under their banner, Saleem Siblings — a brother-and-sister bet on a story that refused to fit a template. "The moment I heard this story, I knew it deserved to be told," Saleem said. "It's original, it's emotional and it keeps you guessing till the very end. You know you're making something that doesn't fit into a familiar template." Backing Qureshi's silent protagonist is a deliciously sturdy ensemble — **Sikandar Kher**, **Chunky Pandey**, the always-magnetic **Seema Pahwa**, Rachit Singh, Vidya Malavade, Himanshu Malik, Marudhar Shekhawat and Arun Kushwah — and Kher promises the fun is in the misdirection: "Nobody in this film is exactly who they appear to be."

Now for the part that'll keep the trade analysts up at night. July 3 is shaping up to be a genuine bloodbath at the box office. **Baby Do Die Do** opens the same Friday as YRF's high-octane spy thriller **Alpha**, starring **Alia Bhatt** and **Sharvari** — two female-led films squaring off head to head, with the global *Minions* juggernaut crowding the multiplexes alongside them. Screen space will be tight, and a smaller, starrier-on-paper rival like Alpha could squeeze Baby's showcount. The smart money says word of mouth, not opening-day muscle, decides this one.

For the diaspora, **Baby Do Die Do** is a theatrical release first — expect it across US, UK, Canada and UAE screens through the usual desi-cinema distributors on July 3, with a streaming home to follow in the months after (an OTT berth hasn't been locked yet, so theatre is your only window for now). If you're the kind of viewer who's tired of the same old shootout choreography, this is the one to watch — a thriller betting everything on a heroine who never raises her voice, and dares you to underestimate her too.

Don't.
